subject: multiple rApache webapps with independent environments?

messages.author: adc05d3187e2b592
messages.subject: multiple rApache webapps with independent environments?
parts:
Hi,

I'm hosting two rApache based webapps on the same server.  One of them has a somewhat long processing step, and during this time I see the variables I generate therein appear in the environment used by my other webapp.  I wasn't expecting this, and as such, the names clobber each other and cause strange errors.

Is this normal?  If so, is there a way to fix this from the rApache side?

Lee

messages.author: 98e634f62928ae87
messages.subject: Re: multiple rApache webapps with independent environments?
parts:
Hi Lee,

as your rApache environment would never be stateful (easily) and your separate webapps would share the same rApache workers at the same time, you should always clean up your environment after each call.

Another workaround would be to start separate Apache instances (on different ports, maybe in a chrooted environment), but with multiple workers you would still have issues even within the same webapp - if you do not clean up the clutter left by the queries.

Maybe calling eval as "secure" with a nice function of Jeroen's RAppArmor would prevent that easily :)

Best,
Gergely

messages.subject: Re: multiple rApache webapps with independent environments?
parts:
Hi Jeff,

My apps both have a ./brew/ directory which is configured with the following:

<DirectoryMatch "^/home/(.+/)?brew">
        SetHandler r-script
        RHandler sys.source
</DirectoryMatch>

Note, I didn't develop these apps to use Rook (didn't know about it when I started).  My apps have generally the same workflow:
  1. upload data file(s)
  2. AJAX call to processing script
  3. process data
  4. return JSON or HTML
Below is the code for the simpler of the two apps.  The other is basically the same but is a bit more complicated (modular via multiple sourced R-scripts).  Notably, variables are being set in .GlobalEnv.

setContentType("text/html")

# process
library(hwriter)

# determine where we are on the server
BASEPATH = sub('/brew/[[:print:]]+?\.R', '', SERVER[['filename']], perl=TRUE)

setwd(BASEPATH)
source('brew/NNKMutationFinderLib.R')

# input arguments
SRC = POST       # this should be explicitly set by the web ui GET has substantial size limitations

ReferenceFile = SRC$ref
ConsensusQualityFile = SRC$cfq
ScoreThresh = as.numeric(SRC$scoreThresh)

OutFile = file.path('data', sub('.fasta', '_nnk_mutations', ReferenceFile, fixed=T))

ref = readFasta('data', ReferenceFile)
ref = sread(ref[1])[[1]]

fq  = readFastq('data', ConsensusQualityFile, withIds=T)

pdf(paste(OutFile, '.pdf', sep='', collapse=''))
tmp = getMutations(fq, ref, qual.thresh = ScoreThresh, graphic=T)
dev.off();

tmp['dna', ] = sapply(tmp['dna', ], function(x){paste(getChangeList(x), collapse=', ')})
tmp['aa', ]  = sapply(tmp['aa', ], function(x){paste(getChangeList(x), collapse=', ')})
tmp = t(tmp)

rn = rownames(tmp)

# order by position in the AA sequence
rex = re.capture('[A-Z*](?<pos>[0-9]+)(?<naa>[A-Z*?])', unlist(tmp[,'aa']))$names
oix = order(ifelse(nchar(rex$pos), as.numeric(rex$pos), NA),
            ifelse(nchar(rex$naa), rex$naa, NA))

tmp = apply(tmp, c(1,2), unlist)
tmp = tmp[oix, ]
tmp = as.data.frame(tmp, stringsAsFactors=F)

tmp$qual.dispersion = sprintf('%.3f', as.numeric(tmp$qual.dispersion))
tmp$qual.quantile = sprintf('%.3f', as.numeric(tmp$qual.quantile))
tmp$qual.score = sprintf('%.3f', as.numeric(tmp$qual.score))

write.csv(tmp, file=paste(OutFile, '.csv', sep='', collapse=''), row.names=T)

scriptTpl = '<script type="text/javascript">$("#ID#").attr("href", "#LINK#")</script>'

cat(sub('#LINK#', paste(OutFile, '.pdf', sep='', collapse=''), sub('#ID#', '#pdffile', scriptTpl, fixed=T), fixed=T))
cat(sub('#LINK#', paste(OutFile, '.csv', sep='', collapse=''), sub('#ID#', '#csvfile', scriptTpl, fixed=T), fixed=T))

cat(hwrite(tmp, border=0))

DONE

When I started getting strange errors I threw together a test script to check the loaded packages and list current variables (from another 'brew' directory):

cat('.libPaths(): ')
print(.libPaths())

cat('.packages() ')
print(.packages())

cat('.GlobalEnv ')
print(ls(.GlobalEnv))

There I saw variables listed from both apps (while they were both running).
I suppose I could try to encapsulate as much as I can into function calls, and rely on post function call garbage collection as Gergely implies.  However, if there is a fix that doesn't require re-architecting my existing code, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Lee

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: multiple rApache webapps with independent environments?
parts:
Hi Lee,

I think I may have introduced this behavior in some recent refactors of rApache. It definitely was not my intention. I'm planning on fixing this in the next release.

In the interim, you can set up your own function that calls sys.source with a new environment every time. The following apache configuration directive will create a function called my.source in the global R environment:

REvalOnStartup "my.source <- function(file=NULL,env=NULL) sys.source(file,envir=new.env(parent=globalenv()))"

Then, you can alter your DirectoryMatch stanza to call my.source rather than sys.source:

<DirectoryMatch "^/home/(.+/)?brew">
        SetHandler r-script
        RHandler my.source
</DirectoryMatch>

Hope this helps,

Jeff

parts: Not yet, and it depends on if you're using rApache like Lee has been with "r-script". But aren't you mainly using handlers?

<jeffrey...@vanderbilt.edu> wrote:
> Hi Lee,
>
> I think I may have introduced this behavior in some recent refactors of
> rApache. It definitely was not my intention. I'm planning on fixing this in
> the next release.
>
> In the interim, you can set up your own function that calls sys.source with
> a new environment every time. The following apache configuration directive
> will create a function called my.source in the global R environment:
>
> REvalOnStartup "my.source <- function(file=NULL,env=NULL)
> sys.source(file,envir=new.env(parent=globalenv()))"
>
> Then, you can alter your DirectoryMatch stanza to call my.source rather than
> sys.source:
>
> <DirectoryMatch "^/home/(.+/)?brew">
>         SetHandler r-script
>         RHandler my.source
> </DirectoryMatch>
>
> Hope this helps,
>
> Jeff
>
> On Tue, Jan 15, 2013 at 5:57 PM, Lee Pang <wlee...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>
>> Hi Jeff,
>>
>> My apps both have a ./brew/ directory which is configured with the
>> following:
>>
>> <DirectoryMatch "^/home/(.+/)?brew">
>>         SetHandler r-script
>>         RHandler sys.source
>> </DirectoryMatch>
>>
>>
>> Note, I didn't develop these apps to use Rook (didn't know about it when I
>> started).  My apps have generally the same workflow:
>>
>> upload data file(s)
>> AJAX call to processing script
>> process data
>> return JSON or HTML
>>
>> Below is the code for the simpler of the two apps.  The other is basically
>> the same but is a bit more complicated (modular via multiple sourced
>> R-scripts).  Notably, variables are being set in .GlobalEnv.
>>
>> setContentType("text/html")
>>
>> # process
>> library(hwriter)
>>
>> # determine where we are on the server
>> BASEPATH = sub('/brew/[[:print:]]+?\\.R', '', SERVER[['filename']],
>> perl=TRUE)
>>
>> setwd(BASEPATH)
>> source('brew/NNKMutationFinderLib.R')
>>
>> # input arguments
>> SRC = POST       # this should be explicitly set by the web ui GET has
>> substantial size limitations
>>
>> ReferenceFile = SRC$ref
>> ConsensusQualityFile = SRC$cfq
>> ScoreThresh = as.numeric(SRC$scoreThresh)
>>
>> OutFile = file.path('data', sub('.fasta', '_nnk_mutations', ReferenceFile,
>> fixed=T))
>>
>> ref = readFasta('data', ReferenceFile)
>> ref = sread(ref[1])[[1]]
>>
>> fq  = readFastq('data', ConsensusQualityFile, withIds=T)
>>
>> pdf(paste(OutFile, '.pdf', sep='', collapse=''))
>> tmp = getMutations(fq, ref, qual.thresh = ScoreThresh, graphic=T)
>> dev.off();
>>
>> tmp['dna', ] = sapply(tmp['dna', ], function(x){paste(getChangeList(x),
>> collapse=', ')})
>> tmp['aa', ]  = sapply(tmp['aa', ], function(x){paste(getChangeList(x),
>> collapse=', ')})
>> tmp = t(tmp)
>>
>> rn = rownames(tmp)
>>
>> # order by position in the AA sequence
>> rex = re.capture('[A-Z*](?<pos>[0-9]+)(?<naa>[A-Z*?])',
>> unlist(tmp[,'aa']))$names
>> oix = order(ifelse(nchar(rex$pos), as.numeric(rex$pos), NA),
>>             ifelse(nchar(rex$naa), rex$naa, NA))
>>
>> tmp = apply(tmp, c(1,2), unlist)
>> tmp = tmp[oix, ]
>> tmp = as.data.frame(tmp, stringsAsFactors=F)
>>
>> tmp$qual.dispersion = sprintf('%.3f', as.numeric(tmp$qual.dispersion))
>> tmp$qual.quantile = sprintf('%.3f', as.numeric(tmp$qual.quantile))
>> tmp$qual.score = sprintf('%.3f', as.numeric(tmp$qual.score))
>>
>> write.csv(tmp, file=paste(OutFile, '.csv', sep='', collapse=''),
>> row.names=T)
>>
>> scriptTpl = '<script type="text/javascript">$("#ID#").attr("href",
>> "#LINK#")</script>'
>>
>> cat(sub('#LINK#', paste(OutFile, '.pdf', sep='', collapse=''), sub('#ID#',
>> '#pdffile', scriptTpl, fixed=T), fixed=T))
>> cat(sub('#LINK#', paste(OutFile, '.csv', sep='', collapse=''), sub('#ID#',
>> '#csvfile', scriptTpl, fixed=T), fixed=T))
>>
>> cat(hwrite(tmp, border=0))
>>
>> DONE
>>
>> When I started getting strange errors I threw together a test script to
>> check the loaded packages and list current variables (from another 'brew'
>> directory):

>> cat('.libPaths():\n')
>> print(.libPaths())
>>
>> cat('.packages()\n')
>> print(.packages())
>>
>> cat('.GlobalEnv\n')
>> print(ls(.GlobalEnv))
>>
>>
>> There I saw variables listed from both apps (while they were both
>> running).
>> I suppose I could try to encapsulate as much as I can into function calls,
>> and rely on post function call garbage collection as Gergely implies.
>> However, if there is a fix that doesn't require re-architecting my existing
>> code, that would be ideal.
>>
>> Thanks,
>> Lee
